question: Can I get credit for courses taken somewhere else?
answer:
smart_toyYes, you can receive credit for courses taken at another institution, provided you follow the established policies and receive prior approval.
To be eligible for off-campus credit, you must adhere to the following guidelines:

Approval Process: You must submit an off-campus request e-form via the Babson Hub, including a course description, syllabus, and rationale. You should wait for approval from the Department of Student Advising & Success before enrolling in the course.
Course Eligibility: Only courses from accredited, degree-granting colleges and universities are considered. The Department of Student Advising & Success will only approve courses that do not overlap with or closely resemble courses offered at Babson.
Credit Limits: Students who matriculated in Fall 2021 or later may take a maximum of 16 credits at another institution (excluding official cross-registration or Babson-approved study abroad/away programs). Students who matriculated prior to Fall 2021 are limited to 12 credits.
Degree Requirements: Off-campus courses are typically awarded as Free Elective or General Elective credit. You must have unsatisfied elective credits available in your degree to apply for off-campus credit.
Grade Requirements: You must earn a grade of C or higher in the approved course for the credits to transfer. These grades will not factor into your cumulative Babson GPA; your transcript will only reflect the credits earned.
Finalizing Credit: To receive the credit, you must have an official transcript sent directly from the institution you attended to the Department of Student Advising & Success.
Financial Responsibility: Babson College tuition does not cover the costs of off-campus courses; any financial obligations are your responsibility.

Please note that you must complete at least one-half of the total credits required for graduation at Babson or through a Babson-affiliated program, regardless of the number of credits accepted from other sources. Additionally, if you are taking courses elsewhere during your final semester, official transcripts must be received by the Registrar by 4:30 pm on the Tuesday before Commencement to meet graduation requirements.
